name: Survival of the Weakest (easy version)
description: This is the easy version of the problem. It differs from the hard one only in constraints on $$$n$$$. You can make hacks only if you lock both versions. Let $$$a_1, a_2, \ldots, a_n$$$ be an array of non-negative integers. Let $$$F(a_1, a_2, \ldots, a_n)$$$ be the sorted in the non-decreasing order array of $$$n - 1$$$ smallest numbers of the form $$$a_i + a_j$$$, where $$$1 \le i \lt j \le n$$$. In other words, $$$F(a_1, a_2, \ldots, a_n)$$$ is the sorted in the non-decreasing order array of $$$n - 1$$$ smallest sums of all possible pairs of elements of the array $$$a_1, a_2, \ldots, a_n$$$. For example, $$$F(1, 2, 5, 7) = [1 + 2, 1 + 5, 2 + 5] = [3, 6, 7]$$$. You are given an array of non-negative integers $$$a_1, a_2, \ldots, a_n$$$. Determine the single element of the array $$$\underbrace{F(F(F\ldots F}_{n-1}(a_1, a_2, \ldots, a_n)\ldots))$$$. Since the answer can be quite large, output it modulo $$$10^9+7$$$.
input_specification: The first line contains one integer $$$n$$$ ($$$2 \le n \le 3000$$$) — the initial length of the array. The second line contains $$$n$$$ integers $$$a_1, a_2, \ldots, a_n$$$ ($$$0 \le a_i \le 10^9$$$) — the array elements.
output_specification: Output a single number — the answer modulo $$$10^9 + 7$$$.
approach_summary: Verify predicate monotonicity: P(x) is true for x ≤ K and false otherwise. Binary search over the answer domain to find the boundary in O(log(Range) × Verify_Time).

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 1805F1 — Survival of the Weakest (easy version) [33. Binary Search]
topic_editorial.summary: Binary search on the monotonic answer domain.
topic_editorial.key_invariant: The predicate function $P(x)$ ('Is answer $\le x$ feasible?') is monotonic: if $P(x)$ is true for some value, it remains true for all larger values (or vice versa). This allows binary division of the answer search space $[\text{low}, \text{high}]$ in $O(\log(\text{Range}))$.
topic_editorial.complexity_analysis:
- **Time Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}(N \log(\text{Range}))$
  The binary search divides the search interval by 2 at each iteration, requiring $\log_2(\text{Range})$ steps. In each step, the feasibility check `check(mid)` scans the array in $\mathcal{O}(N)$ time.
- **Space Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}(1)$ auxiliary space
  The algorithm operates directly over the input array without allocating extra auxiliary memory.
